academic_credits: No academic credit for independent OCW learners
scope_notes: Graduate entrepreneurship course on opportunity identification, market segmentation, customer research, competitive positioning, product planning, go-to-market, sales, finance, team formation and legal/organizational issues, built around developing a startup business plan and investor pitch.
prerequisites: No formal OCW prerequisite stated, but the original MIT course was designed for graduate learners building technology-based ventures
required_resources: General-purpose computer and browser; spreadsheet use is helpful for the financial template; no paid platform is required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course is explicitly learn-by-doing: students progress through venture creation by building the essential parts of a business plan and investor pitch rather than only studying entrepreneurship concepts.
component_evidence.depth: A semester-length graduate course covers customer discovery, market sizing, competition, product, sales, finance, people and legal/organizational issues at substantial depth.
component_evidence.practice: Twelve assignments, evaluation sheets, financial templates and a final business-plan structure provide unusually strong applied practice for an openly available entrepreneurship course.
component_evidence.materials: OCW exposes syllabus, calendar, readings, lecture notes, tutorial videos, assignments, evaluation sheets and downloadable course files in a highly complete package.
component_evidence.currency: The course was taught in Spring 2013. Core opportunity/customer and venture-planning methods remain valuable, but startup financing, legal context, digital distribution and contemporary venture-building practice have changed materially.
component_evidence.expertise: William Aulet, Howard Anderson and Matt Marx bring strong MIT Sloan entrepreneurship, venture and strategy expertise.
component_evidence.accessibility: All materials are open and downloadable, but the graduate, technology-venture orientation and substantial project workload raise the entry barrier.

recommendation_rationale: An outstanding project-heavy entrepreneurship course for durable startup fundamentals, but its 2013 venture ecosystem and legal/finance context require modern supplementation. Prefer newer alternatives for a current all-in-one startup playbook.

academic_credits: No academic credit for independent OCW learners
scope_notes: Current MIT IAP entrepreneurship course covering customer identification, venture/business models, sales, people and organizational issues, legal issues, negotiation, financing sources, financial projections and common startup mistakes through practitioner-led sessions.
prerequisites: No formal prerequisite stated; designed for learners considering for-profit, social or development ventures
required_resources: General-purpose computer and browser; no paid platform or specialist software required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The compact course is organized around concrete startup execution problems and practitioner-led sessions, moving from customer discovery through business model, people/legal issues, negotiation, finance and common failure modes.
component_evidence.depth: Six core sessions provide a broad practical startup toolkit, but the compressed IAP format is less deep than a semester-long venture-development course.
component_evidence.practice: The public OCW route is rich in worked practitioner examples and decision frameworks but exposes little formal learner assessment or project structure compared with MIT 15.390.
component_evidence.materials: OCW provides lecture videos, notes, readings, editable files and current venture resources in a coherent downloadable package.
component_evidence.currency: The course was taught in January 2025, and OCW added an additional innovation session in 2026, giving unusually strong currentness for entrepreneurship.
component_evidence.expertise: Joseph Hadzima and invited speakers have direct venture-launch, legal, financing and operating experience, giving the course strong practitioner authority.
component_evidence.accessibility: All materials are open and self-paced, with no credential or paid account requirement and limited formal prerequisites.

recommendation_rationale: One of the best current free startup-execution courses: concise, practitioner-led and unusually fresh. It is less practice-intensive than MIT 15.390 or OpenLearn's structured badged route, but stronger on contemporary startup execution.

credential: Free Open University Statement of Participation and digital badge after completing the course and required quizzes
academic_credits: No academic credit for the OpenLearn route; 24 CPD points are available as continuing-professional-development evidence
scope_notes: Twenty-four-hour, eight-session entrepreneurship course covering idea generation, entrepreneur capability, business models, customers and markets, value proposition, resources and capabilities, finance, business structures, risk, growth, networks and pitching.
prerequisites: No formal prerequisites; Level 2 intermediate course suitable for aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs
required_resources: Browser; free OpenLearn account for progress, quizzes, activities and rewards; downloadable Word, PDF, EPUB and other formats are available

component_evidence.pedagogy: The eight-session sequence follows the venture journey from ideas through business model, customers, value proposition, resources, finance, growth and pitching, using case studies and practical entrepreneur advice.
component_evidence.depth: Twenty-four hours provides meaningful breadth across the core early-stage entrepreneurship decisions while remaining accessible to non-specialists.
component_evidence.practice: Interactive quizzes, compulsory badge quizzes, case-based activities, a Business Model Canvas, profit-and-loss resources and pitch-building tasks create strong applied practice with automated feedback.
component_evidence.materials: OpenLearn provides structured text, case studies, downloadable formats, business tools, quizzes, references and further reading in a highly complete package.
component_evidence.currency: The course was formally updated on 3 March 2026, a strong currentness signal for startup practice and business-model content.
component_evidence.expertise: The Open University combines academic business education with practitioner case material and continuing-professional-development design.
component_evidence.accessibility: The content can be started without sign-up, is fully free, self-paced and downloadable; a free account unlocks quizzes, tracking, badge and Statement of Participation.

recommendation_rationale: The strongest general entrepreneurship recommendation in the current survivor pool: current, structured, practice-rich and accessible without sacrificing useful depth. MIT 15.393 is better for a compact practitioner-led startup perspective; MIT 15.390 is deeper but dated.

credential: Free Saylor course-completion certificate; optional ACE-recommended credit exam uses a separate paid proctoring route
academic_credits: ACE-recommended credit is available only through the optional separately proctored route
scope_notes: Thirty-eight-hour operations-management course spanning operations strategy, product and process design, supply-chain management, lean/JIT systems, capacity and facility layout, work systems, inventory and quality management.
required_resources: Web-capable device, internet and free Saylor account for assessments and certificate; optional mobile offline access

component_evidence.pedagogy: The nine-unit sequence progresses from operations strategy into process, supply chain, lean, capacity, inventory and quality, with repeated self-testing and application-oriented outcomes.
component_evidence.depth: Thirty-eight hours covers the main undergraduate operations-management domains with meaningful breadth.
component_evidence.practice: Auto-graded unit assessments and a free final exam provide regular checking, though the public route exposes less project-based operational analysis than a case-heavy university course.
component_evidence.materials: Saylor curates articles, lectures and videos into a complete structured course; source consistency is lower than a single-faculty course but coverage is broad.
component_evidence.currency: The syllabus was last modified on 2 October 2025, an important currentness signal for supply-chain, lean and operations practice.
component_evidence.expertise: Saylor's faculty-reviewed open curriculum is credible, though course-level instructor expertise is less transparent than named university faculty.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course, assessments and certificate are free and self-paced; optional ACE proctoring is clearly separate.

recommendation_rationale: A strong, current and substantial free operations-management foundation with assessment and a certificate. It is the clear survivor for this subtopic after shallower or older alternatives were removed at screening.

credential: Free Saylor course-completion certificate after the free final exam
academic_credits: No academic credit verified for the free route
scope_notes: Thirty-nine-hour five-unit entrepreneurship foundation covering opportunity viability, team building, business planning, marketing strategy, accounting/tax basics, venture finance, growth and exit strategies.
required_resources: Web-capable device, internet and free Saylor account for assessments and certificate

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course follows a logical venture-building sequence from entrepreneurship fundamentals and teams into business planning, marketing and financing, with explicit learning outcomes and self-testing.
component_evidence.depth: Thirty-nine hours gives solid breadth across small-business and entrepreneurship fundamentals, although each functional area remains introductory.
component_evidence.practice: Unit assessments and a free final exam support retention; the course teaches business-plan construction but exposes less authentic project execution than MIT 15.390 or OpenLearn's activity-rich route.
component_evidence.materials: Saylor curates textbooks, videos, webpages and activities into a complete structured path, though source uniformity is mixed.
component_evidence.currency: The syllabus was last modified on 2 October 2025, providing a strong currentness signal for entrepreneurship, marketing and financing content.
component_evidence.expertise: The curriculum is faculty-reviewed and structured, but named specialist entrepreneurship faculty are less visible than in MIT or Open University alternatives.
component_evidence.accessibility: The full course, assessments and certificate are free, self-paced and require no specialist software.

recommendation_rationale: A strong conventional entrepreneurship course with current maintenance and free certification. OpenLearn is the better general recommendation because its case studies, interactive tasks and 2026 update produce a richer learner experience.

credential: Free HP LIFE Certificate of Completion
scope_notes: Compact leadership microcourse on leadership versus management, leadership strategies, team building, communication, organizational change, ethics, self-awareness and developing a personal leadership philosophy.
prerequisites: No formal prerequisites; intended for broad workforce and entrepreneurship learners
required_resources: Browser or HP LIFE mobile app and free learner account; no paid software required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course uses a concise skills-oriented progression and a self-awareness quiz to connect leadership concepts to personal strengths, weaknesses and a leadership philosophy.
component_evidence.depth: HP LIFE courses are designed as short stand-alone modules of roughly 30–60 minutes, so the course can only introduce leadership concepts rather than develop them deeply.
component_evidence.practice: A short self-assessment/quiz adds active reflection, but there is little evidence of extended scenarios, projects, coached practice or sustained team-leadership exercises.
component_evidence.materials: The module is clear and accessible within HP LIFE, but its intentionally compact format provides fewer substantial learning assets than longer leadership courses.
component_evidence.currency: HP LIFE announced the current Effective Leadership course in January 2024 and continues actively promoting it in 2026, so its workplace framing is current.
component_evidence.expertise: HP Foundation provides credible workforce-skills training, though course-level named leadership faculty and research grounding are less transparent than Open University alternatives.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course is free, very short, mobile-accessible, multilingual at platform level and includes a free completion certificate.

recommendation_rationale: A useful ultra-low-friction leadership primer, but it is a microcourse rather than a serious leadership-development pathway. OpenLearn Leadership and followership should be preferred when the learner can invest more time.

credential: No free formal completion credential verified for the open-access route; course quiz is freely accessible
scope_notes: Four-hour French-language introduction to running a first project from objectives and planning through day-to-day steering, team coordination, evaluation and communicating results.
required_resources: Modern browser and free OpenClassrooms access; no specialist software or paid service required for core course content

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course is organised around one concrete outcome—piloting a first project end to end—and translates concepts into a simple sequence of planning, steering and evaluation steps.
component_evidence.depth: Four hours provides a useful beginner orientation but cannot cover project-management methods, risk, budgeting, stakeholder management and delivery frameworks at substantial depth.
component_evidence.practice: The route includes practical tools and a cumulative quiz, providing more application than passive content but less sustained practice than Saylor BUS402.
component_evidence.materials: OpenClassrooms provides a focused, professionally produced sequence with a clear syllabus and practical method framing.
component_evidence.currency: The course was updated on 4 December 2025, giving a strong currentness signal.
component_evidence.expertise: Instructor Pierre-Benoît Lagoeyte is a project manager, instructional designer and adult trainer with more than a decade of relevant experience.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course is free/open-access, only four hours, has no prerequisites and is delivered in French, providing useful language diversity.

recommendation_rationale: The best low-friction French introduction to project management in the pool, but Saylor BUS402 is far deeper and should be preferred for a full foundation.

credential: No free formal completion credential verified for the open-access route; module quizzes are freely accessible
scope_notes: Eight-hour practical people-management course on entering a management role, adapting management style, delegation, meetings, communication, goals, performance monitoring, reviews, feedback, motivation, prioritisation, recruitment and onboarding.
prerequisites: No formal prerequisites stated; designed for new or aspiring managers
required_resources: Modern browser and free OpenClassrooms access; no specialist software required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The three-part toolbox follows the daily manager journey from organizing team work to performance support and hiring/onboarding, keeping concepts tied to concrete managerial actions.
component_evidence.depth: Eight hours offers useful operational breadth for new managers but does not reach the theory, reflection or longitudinal development depth of a 24-hour leadership programme.
component_evidence.practice: Three section quizzes and scenario-oriented management tasks create regular applied checking, although there is no extended coached leadership project.
component_evidence.materials: The course provides a coherent practical toolkit with clearly structured lessons and assessment checkpoints.
component_evidence.currency: The course was updated on 23 January 2025 and addresses current management workflows and team practices.
component_evidence.expertise: The named instructors bring management, innovation, business-development, advisory and mentoring experience.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course is free/open-access, self-paced, only eight hours and requires no specialist tools or formal prerequisites.

recommendation_rationale: A strong practical toolbox for new managers. It is more immediately operational than OpenLearn Leadership and followership, but the OpenLearn course is deeper, more reflective and better as a general leadership-development recommendation.

credential: Free Open University digital badge and Statement of Participation after completing the course and required quizzes
academic_credits: No academic credit for the OpenLearn route; 24 CPD points are available as continuing-professional-development evidence
scope_notes: Twenty-four-hour, eight-week leadership-development course covering leadership and followership concepts, styles, context, skills, common challenges, future leadership, reflective practice, leadership journaling and a personal action plan.
prerequisites: No formal prerequisites; Level 1 introductory course for aspiring or current leaders
required_resources: Browser and optional free OpenLearn account for tracking, quizzes, activities, badge and statement; downloadable Word, PDF, EPUB and other formats are available

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course combines academic leadership theory with reflection, case material, weekly quizzes, a leadership journal and a personal development plan, creating a coherent theory-to-self-development progression.
component_evidence.depth: Eight weeks at roughly three hours per week gives meaningful breadth across leadership styles, context, followership, challenges and future leadership while remaining introductory.
component_evidence.practice: Weekly quizzes, reflective activities, self-assessment, leadership journaling and an action plan provide sustained practice directly tied to personal leadership development.
component_evidence.materials: OpenLearn supplies videos, structured readings, references, a toolkit, downloadable formats, quizzes and continuing-professional-development resources.
component_evidence.currency: The course was first published and updated on 2 January 2024 and explicitly addresses technological developments, global change and emerging leadership styles.
component_evidence.expertise: The Open University combines academic leadership research with professional-development pedagogy and CPD accreditation.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course is fully free, self-paced, downloadable, beginner-friendly and provides a free badge and Statement of Participation.

recommendation_rationale: The strongest general leadership-development route in the current pool: substantial, reflective, practice-rich and accessible. OpenClassrooms is better for a compact new-manager toolbox; Saylor Ethical Leadership is a narrower ethics complement.

credential: Free Saylor course-completion certificate; optional ACE-recommended credit exam uses a separate paid proctoring route
academic_credits: ACE-recommended college credit available only through the optional separately proctored route
scope_notes: Fifty-two-hour project-management foundation spanning initiating, planning, executing, monitoring/controlling and closing process groups plus project-manager people skills and PMI Talent Triangle framing.
required_resources: Web-capable device, internet and free Saylor account for assessments and certificate; optional mobile offline access

component_evidence.pedagogy: The five-unit course follows the full project life cycle and integrates process knowledge with people skills, giving learners a coherent start-to-finish project-management structure.
component_evidence.depth: Fifty-two hours provides substantial foundation-level depth across project phases, terminology, tools and interpersonal competencies.
component_evidence.practice: Auto-graded assessments and a free final exam create repeated checking; the route is less simulation- or capstone-heavy than experiential project programmes.
component_evidence.materials: Saylor curates open readings, videos and activities into a full course with syllabus, assessments and current project-management terminology.
component_evidence.currency: The syllabus was last modified on 2 October 2025 and explicitly references PMI's current Talent Triangle framing, supporting strong currentness.
component_evidence.expertise: Saylor provides a structured faculty-reviewed curriculum, though named project-management instructor expertise is less transparent than PMI-authored training.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course, assessments and certificate are free and self-paced; optional paid ACE proctoring is clearly separated from the core route.

recommendation_rationale: The strongest long-form project-management foundation among current discovery survivors. OpenClassrooms is a better four-hour French primer, while PMI KICKOFF remains a strong reference-fixture option for a much shorter authoritative introduction.
